general_information.Description: This course provides fundamental concepts, principles, and rules concerning different types of intellectual property rights relating to graphic design and/or multimedia communication, particularly copyright, trademark, and registered design. Students will learn how to apply these principles and rules to protect their intellectual property rights in relation to their graphic design works and/or multimedia communication work. During the course, there are several typical cases regarding intellectual property rights relevant to graphic designs and/or multimedia communication available for students to analyze and discuss. Students are also provided with basic skills such as how to acquire intellectual property protection for their creative products, how to avoid infringing on other people's intellectual property rights when creating new works, and how to commercialize their intellectual property rights. In addition to common teaching methods such as lectures, brainstorming, and group discussion, the instructor will also use teaching methods specific to law, such as case studies, problem-solving, and moot court exercises.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises and assignments given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand the basic rules and doctrines regulating different types of intellectual property rights in connection with graphic design and/or multimedia communication
Apply the aforesaid basic rules and doctrines to protect their intellectual property rights relating to their creative works
Understand elements of some typical infringements of intellectual property rights in connection with graphic design and/or multimedia communication
Be able to discover infringement and take action against a person who infringes on their intellectual property rights relating to their design and/or multimedia communication
Understand legal issues related to licensing
Apply knowledge to negotiate, draft, and perform licensing agreements to transfer intellectual property rights to others
Be able to study relevant laws independently to prevent infringement of others’ intellectual property rights
Understand how to take action against infringers

assessments.Grading Guide: In class and home conducted from assinged topic until oral presentation '- Students will work in teams of 4–5 to research a company, design a brand identity (including logo, color palette, typography, and visual style), and prepare a legal analysis to ensure the proposed identity is free from copyright or trademark conflicts. The final deliverables will include a design portfolio, a written report, and a group presentation. Phase 1: Research & Analysis 'Goal: Understand the company and its branding context. Tasks: - Select or create a company (real or fictional). - Research its mission, target audience, competitors, and market positioning. - Study other existing brand identities in the same industry. - Begin exploring legal frameworks: copyright, trademark, and brand protection. AI Applications: -Use AI to summarize company profiles and competitor analysis. - Ask AI to explain branding trends and legal concepts in simple terms. - Generate SWOT analysis or brand positioning maps. Phase 2: Design & Report Writing (self-handling by group of students) Goal: Create the brand identity and justify its legal safety. Tasks: - Design logo, color palette, typography, and visual style. - Prepare mockups (e.g., packaging, website, business cards). - Write a report including: + Brand rationale + Legal analysis (trademark search, copyright considerations) + Justification of originality and legal safety. Phase 3: Presentation & Defense Goal: Pitch the brand identity and defend its legal validity. Tasks: - Deliver a 10-minute group presentation. - Explain the design concept and legal analysis. - Respond to questions and challenges from peers or instructors. AI Applications: - Use AI to generate slide outlines and talking points.

-Students will write an in-class essay that demonstrates their understanding of key legal principles related to Intellectual Property Rights (any perspective as decided by the instructor); - The essay question will be provided at the time of the test and will reflect a prominent, timely issue in intellectual property Students must respond with a well-structured essay that includes: - A clear thesis or position - Legal reasoning and relevant examples - Reflection on fairness, impact, or ethical considerations - Essays must be written individually, during class time, without external assistance.
